comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PLAN-REVIEW: BLOCK, 9 blocking findings — and the gate is RIGHT. I wrote the Approach as "candidate, not
a decision" and deferred the primary design decision to whoever implements it. That is a placeholder, not
a plan, and it must be resolved before this is claimable. Recording the findings and one genuinely NEW
discovery so the design work is scoped rather than rediscovered.

NEW FINDING FROM THE REVIEW, VERIFIED: a THIRD gate has the same inversion, and my plan never named it.
`completion.py:332` reads:
    if cfg.model == DEFAULT_MODEL:
        cfg = replace(cfg, model=_VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL)
That is the same equality test as `review_kernel/verify.py:269`, on a SEPARATE code path (the completion
verifier's own downgrade). So on any non-default model — every Bedrock id — the completion verifier ALSO
stops downgrading to sonnet and follows cfg.model. Affected gates are therefore THREE, not two:
plan-review (via _verifier_cfg), code-review (which has no downgrade at all), and completion.
Note what sits immediately below that line: a `temperature=0` greedy pin added for bug e458, justified as
"an unpinned temperature runs at the provider default (~1.0), whose sampling variance flips borderline
judgments". That is the same determinism property ticket 1903 showed is silently lost on opus-4-8 — so a
non-default-model run can lose BOTH the sonnet downgrade AND the greedy pin on the same path.

THE DESIGN DECISIONS THIS PLAN MUST MAKE (currently all deferred):
1. The replacement semantics for `resolve_verifier_model`. The current rule conflates "the operator chose
   a model" with "the model is not the framework default". State the intended rule positively: what
   distinguishes an explicit operator override from a provider change, given both arrive as cfg.model?
2. The SCHEMA of the per-provider mapping: key vocabulary (how a provider is named), value shape
   (pass-name -> model-id? a ladder per pass?), and where it lives (YAML gate file, config table, code).
3. The DATA-FLOW: how a provider-prefixed id reaches the batch runners. The YAML `model_ladder` is a
   static list of bare strings flowing unchanged into `production_batch_runner`/`code_review.batch_runner`;
   the plan must say how per-provider values get there, and how they interact with `resolve_model`'s
   step > workflow > config precedence and code-review.yaml's per-step `model:` key.
4. A ROLLBACK/SAFETY story. The Anthropic path MEASURABLY works today (41 opus + 1 sonnet on a real run).
   Changing verify.py:269 and the model_ladder risks that working behaviour, and the plan offers no
   revert path or guard.
5. AC4 is unfalsifiable as written ("expresses its per-pass models explicitly") — no artifact, no command,
   and "explicitly" is subjective. Name the observable: which config key, or which grep, proves it.
6. Positive rationale for "configuration keyed by provider" over the alternatives (e.g. runtime
   provider-aware resolution at the seam, or per-pass model ids carried on the gate YAML). The review
   correctly notes two structurally different options exist and the plan argues for neither.

STATUS: NOT claimable. This needs a real design pass, not an implementation pass. It is also the highest-
leverage ticket in the epic — it blocks BOTH 0d76 (S6) and eb6e (S8) — so the design work is the critical
path, and doing it badly would be worse than doing it slowly.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
CHECKED FOR SUPERSESSION BY eb58, and this ticket is NOT superseded — recording the check so the next agent does not re-open the question or, worse, skip the ticket as redundant.

The suspicion was reasonable: eb58 (Model classes: trivial/standard/frontier) just closed with all six children done, and THIS ticket's problem statement says "there is no way to express [per-pass models] on any non-default provider" — which sounds like exactly what eb58 delivered.

The distinction is MECHANISM vs CONSUMER:
* eb58 delivered the mechanism — per-class slots (`[tool.rebar.llm.model_classes]`), the nine `REBAR_LLM_<CLASS>_<FIELD>` overrides, per-class fallback chains, class-aware resolution, and the REBAR_LLM_MODEL deprecation/fan-out.
* THIS ticket makes the GATES actually USE it per pass. Verified against the shipped YAML: the code-review gate's `verify` step already declares `model: standard` (landed by 172e), but `base` (Pass-1) and `coach` (Pass-4) still inherit `cfg.model` implicitly. Nothing in eb58 changed those.
* Its ACs also demand things eb58 does not assert: that the RESOLVED model per pass is the intended class under a BEDROCK configuration, and that no bare `claude-*` id resolves to provider `anthropic` during a run configured for another provider. Those are cross-provider resolution guarantees, not class-plumbing.

So eb58 is a PREREQUISITE that is now satisfied, which is why this ticket became ready. `rebar ready` lists it as unblocked.

METHOD NOTE while I am here: I initially read this ticket's `deps` field (and 8625's) as the blocker list and concluded 8625 had none. WRONG — `deps` was `[]` on 8625 while the plan-review precheck correctly refused it as "blocked by unclosed ticket(s) eb58, eb6e". Blocking comes from LINK relations, not that field. `rebar ready` is the authoritative claimability check. The gate fast-failed with NO LLM spend, so the misread cost nothing — that fast-fail is doing real work.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PRE-IMPLEMENTATION CORRECTION TO THIS PLAN'S OWN CLASS TABLE — apply after round 3 returns (comment, not an edit, because a review is in flight). Found by reading the batch execution path BEFORE claiming, not by discovering it mid-implementation.

**THE TABLE I JUST ADDED SPECIFIES `model: frontier` FOR `round_a` AND `round_b`. THAT WOULD BE A SILENT NO-OP.** Those two are BATCH steps, and the batch path never reads a step-level `model:`:
* `workflow/interpreter.py:384-395` builds `BatchRunRequest` from the `batch:` sub-dict ONLY — `finder=batch['prompt']`, `usd_budget=batch.get('usd_budget')`, `model_ladder=tuple(batch.get('model_ladder') or ())`. The enclosing step's `model:` key is never passed in.
* `workflow/runners.py:128-130` then computes `model = resolve_model_string(req.model_ladder[0]) if req.model_ladder else None`, and its own comment states the consequence explicitly: "an EMPTY ladder still yields None — 'no per-step model', NOT a resolved class."
So `model: frontier` on a batch step would parse fine (`model` IS in schema.py's `_STEP_ORDER`, so no validation error) and be silently discarded — `round_a`/`round_b` would keep inheriting `cfg.model`, the exact defect this ticket exists to remove. Worse, a test written as "the YAML declares a class for every LLM step" would PASS while the runtime behaviour was unchanged.

**CORRECTED TABLE — the two batch steps take a SINGLE-RUNG LADDER, which is the key the batch path actually reads:**
    base     :67   Pass-1 single-shot   step-level  `model: frontier`
    round_a  :77   Pass-1 batch         inside batch: `model_ladder: [frontier]`
    round_b  :109  Pass-1 batch         inside batch: `model_ladder: [frontier]`
    verify   :143  Pass-2               `model: standard` — ALREADY LANDED (172e)
    coach    :182  Pass-4 single-shot   step-level  `model: standard`

A ONE-RUNG LADDER ALSO PRESERVES THE DETERMINISM ARGUMENT the plan already makes for rejecting plan-review's `[trivial, standard, frontier]`: with a single rung there is no escalation, so the resolved model per criterion is determinate and the AC's "resolved model for each pass is the intended class" test stays writable. And `resolve_model_string` maps the rung `frontier` through the class table (7761), so it follows the RUN's provider rather than a hardcoded Anthropic id — which is the whole point under a Bedrock config.

TEST CONSEQUENCE, so the test cannot pass vacuously: assert the RESOLVED model reaching each step at RUNTIME, not merely that the YAML carries a class token. A YAML-only assertion is exactly what would have hidden this bug.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
**CONFIRMED DEFECT IN THIS TICKET'S OWN IMPLEMENTATION — DO NOT CLOSE 3768. The change is a NO-OP at runtime for the code-review gate, and my tests did not catch it.**

EVIDENCE, from a real gate run with per-call logging (`REBAR_USAGE_LOG`, which records one JSON object per LLM call at the runner chokepoint — `runner.py:545`):
    rebar -c verify.enable_code_review=true review-code --base HEAD~2 --head HEAD~1
    REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE=<inverted>.toml   REBAR_USAGE_LOG=<jsonl>
Config (INVERTED on purpose): frontier=`bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`, standard=`anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`.
Six per-call records, ALL on `anthropic:claude-opus-4-8` (provider=anthropic):
    code-review-base                            in=787,803
    code-review-docs                            in= 22,052
    code-review-tests                           in=699,425
    code-review-deletion-impact                 in= 98,838
    code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries in= 22,168
    code-review-api-compat                      in=330,696
`base` declares `model: frontier`, which under this config MUST resolve to `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`. It resolved to the bare default instead. So the declaration is not reaching the resolver.

**BOTH COMPETING EXPLANATIONS WERE TESTED — this is not an inference from one observation.**
* H2 "the config pointer was not loaded, so `frontier` fell back to its BUILT-IN default (also claude-opus-4-8)" would produce the IDENTICAL log. ELIMINATED: with the same env var, `load_class_slots()` -> `resolve_class('frontier')` returns `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`, both with and without `repo_root=` (the form the gate uses).
* H1 "the step's `model:` never reaches `resolve_model`" is therefore what remains. Corroborated: `resolve_model(cfg, step='frontier')` -> `bedrock:...` but `resolve_model(cfg, step=None)` -> `claude-opus-4-8`, which is exactly what was observed.
ALSO RULED OUT: the running package loads MY worktree gate — `rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` under rebar-wt-provider-seam, with all five declarations intact — and `code_review/shim.py:119 review_code` really does execute the gate via `gate_dispatch.produce_code_review_verdict`.

**WHY MY 9 TESTS PASSED ANYWAY — the honest post-mortem.** They assert two things: (1) the YAML carries the right class token in the right place, and (2) `resolve_model_string(<that token>)` resolves correctly under a Bedrock config. Neither asserts THE ENGINE PASSES THE TOKEN TO THE RESOLVER DURING A RUN. That is precisely the gap this plan's own text warns about — "assert the RESOLVED model reaching each step at RUNTIME, never merely that the YAML carries a class token" — and I did not actually do it. The 6/6 mutation results are consistent with that: every mutation I ran perturbed the YAML or the class table, so every one was caught by a YAML/resolution assertion. No mutation could distinguish "declaration honoured" from "declaration ignored", because no test observes the runtime binding.

NEXT STEPS (do not close until these are done):
1. Find where the code-review gate's step model is (not) plumbed. `CodeReviewBatchRunner` (`code_review/batch_runner.py:60-61,83-84`) DOES resolve `req.model_ladder[0]` and set `step['model']`, so the batch path looks correct in isolation — determine whether `interpreter.py:388` is even the constructor used for this gate, and how `base` (a single-shot prompt step) reaches `runs.py:154`'s `resolve_model(cfg, step=ctx.step.get('model'), ...)`.
2. Add an END-TO-END test that would have caught this: execute the gate with a RECORDING runner and assert the model each step receives. Deterministic, free, and strictly stronger than the live probe.
3. Only then re-run the live probe as the [operator-attested] evidence.

The Gerrit change 1169 is +1/+1 and submittable, but it should NOT be treated as delivering the behaviour until this is fixed — it currently ships YAML that the runtime ignores.

The run finished with NINE per-call records (`REBAR_USAGE_LOG`). EVERY ONE on `anthropic:claude-opus-4-8`, under a config where frontier=`bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` and standard=`anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`:
    1 code-review-base                             opus   (mine: model: frontier)
    2 code-review-docs                             opus   (batch criterion)
    3 code-review-tests                            opus   (batch criterion)
    4 code-review-deletion-impact                  opus   (batch criterion)
    5 code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries  opus   (batch criterion)
    6 code-review-api-compat                       opus   (batch criterion)
    7 code-review-verify                           opus   <-- **172e's `model: standard`, NOT my change**
    8 code-review-coach                            opus   (mine: model: standard)
    9 code-novelty                                 opus

`verify` (`code-review.yaml:171`) has declared `model: standard` since story 172e closed. Under this config that MUST resolve to `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`. It resolved to opus. **That declaration predates my change entirely**, which means the code-review gate has never honoured a per-step model declaration — this is NOT a regression I introduced, and it is not fixable by editing the YAML.

CONSEQUENCES, stated plainly:
1. **My 3768 change is correct in FORM but INERT**, and so is 172e's. The YAML is right; the runtime ignores it. Gerrit 1169 is +1/+1 but must not be read as delivering the behaviour.
2. **This ticket's real scope is the PLUMBING, not the declarations.** Its own Problem section says "Code review is only PARTLY split" on the strength of `verify` declaring a class — that premise is now falsified: the split does not exist AT ALL at runtime, because no declaration is honoured.
3. **172e closed with this latent.** Its criterion "each of the three verifier paths resolves the `standard` class" was evidently satisfied by unit tests over the resolution helpers rather than by an observed runtime binding — the same gap that let my 9 tests pass. Worth a follow-up ticket rather than a silent fix here; I am not filing one unilaterally.
4. The `[operator-attested]` criterion CANNOT be satisfied yet, and should not be. The honest reading of this run is that it DISPROVES the behaviour the criterion asks me to demonstrate. Its failure was the gate doing its job.

WHY EVERY CHEAPER PROBE WOULD HAVE MISLED, recorded because the discrimination mattered three times:
* The caching-warning lines captured only 3 of 9 calls (they fire only when caching was requested and had no effect), so my first extraction under-sampled and I wrongly announced, then retracted, a conclusion drawn from 3/8.
* A NON-inverted config would have shown `anthropic:claude-opus-4-8` for a working frontier class too — identical to inheritance — so it could not have detected this at all.
* "Config not loaded" was eliminated separately: with the same env var, `load_class_slots()`/`resolve_class('frontier')` returns `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`, with and without `repo_root=`.

NEXT: find where the code-review gate drops `step['model']` (compare against the plan-review path, which demonstrably DOES honour classes — its 41/1 opus/sonnet split was observed live on eb58), fix the plumbing, then add an end-to-end test that asserts the model each step RECEIVES via a recording runner. Only after that is the live attestation meaningful.

This is the ticket's final [operator-attested] criterion: "a real gate run **on the non-default
provider** shows the per-pass model ids actually used, cited from the run's usage log in a comment."

**Run:** `rebar review-code --base HEAD~1 --head HEAD` (attested source) on commit 2e17171e5c, from a
build carrying story b690's fix, `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` enabled. All three classes on **Bedrock**, while

PROVIDER as well as model:

    cfg.model = claude-opus-4-8              -> provider anthropic  (what a dropped declaration hits)
    frontier  = bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8
    standard  = bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6

    step      op                                            model_class  model
    ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    base      code-review-base                              frontier     bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8
    round_a   code-review-docs                              frontier     bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8
    round_a   code-review-tests                             frontier     bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8
    round_a   code-review-deletion-impact                   frontier     bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8
    round_a   code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries    frontier     bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8
    verify    code-review-verify                            standard     bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6
    coach     code-review-coach                             standard     bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6
    (none)    code-novelty                                  (none)       anthropic:claude-opus-4-8

    verdict: PASS   llm_ran: True   llm_error: None

**WHAT THIS SATISFIES.** All FIVE LLM-calling steps ran on the class the YAML declares, on a
non-default provider — `base` (`model: frontier`), `round_a`/`round_b` (`batch.model_ladder`),
`verify` and `coach` (`model: standard`, `verify`'s landed by 172e). It also satisfies this ticket's
sibling criterion "no bare `claude-*` model id is resolved to provider `anthropic` during a run
configured for another provider" — for every classed step. The `round_b` step is absent from THIS run
because Round-B membership is escalation-driven and the base reviewer recommended no overlays; its
declaration is covered live by the anthropic run recorded on b690 and offline by

**WHAT IT DOES NOT SATISFY — stated rather than glossed.** The last row is a LEAK: the `code-novelty`
sub-call ran on **direct Anthropic** while every classed step was on Bedrock. It is not a workflow
step (hence no `step`/`model_class`), it passes `config=cfg` with no class, and so it inherits

provider" holds for the STEPS but NOT for the whole run. Filed as **afeb** (parented to epic 061c)
rather than folded in here, because it is a different seam — and it matters beyond this ticket: it
means a Bedrock cutover (eb6e) is not actually complete, and it sends the diff and prior findings to
direct Anthropic.

**A SECOND FINDING FROM THE SAME EXERCISE.** The first two attempts at this evidence used the
CANONICAL Bedrock id form (`us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`) and could not run at all:
`_resolve_target`'s "already provider-qualified" test is `":" in model`, and a versioned Bedrock id
contains a colon in its version suffix, so the configured `provider = "bedrock"` was silently dropped
and the id was then misread as `provider = "us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1"`. The gate
degraded to INDETERMINATE. Filed as **03b0**. This run therefore uses the UNVERSIONED aliases
(`us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`, `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`) as a deliberate workaround — worth
knowing when reading the table above, because the evidence is real but was obtained around a bug.

**PREREQUISITE NOTE.** This evidence was impossible before b690: the `step` and `model_class` columns
did not exist, and `op` alone cannot attribute a call to a pass. b690 is `LLM-Review +1` /
`Verified +1` as Gerrit 1178 (not submitted — the stack lands when epic 061c closes).

compiled_state.description:
# A per-pass model configuration seam (one env var cannot express four passes)

## Problem

rebar's gates deliberately run different model classes per pass. On the direct-Anthropic path this
works today and is MEASURED: a real `rebar review-plan` made 41 calls on `anthropic:claude-opus-4-8`
(Pass-1, which escalates up from the YAML `model_ladder`) and 1 on `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`
(the Pass-2/Pass-4 verifier downgrade). The operator requirement is exactly that shape: Pass-1 on
opus for most criteria, Pass-2/Pass-4 on sonnet.

There is no way to express that on any non-default provider, because the whole selection collapses
onto ONE knob:

- ~~**The verifier downgrade inverts.**~~ **RESOLVED — retained only so the record shows what changed.**
  This bullet argued that `review_kernel/verify.py:269`'s `verifier_default if model == default_model
  else (model or verifier_default)` would read ANY Bedrock id as an explicit operator choice, so the
  sonnet downgrade would stop applying and Pass-2/Pass-4 would follow Pass-1 onto one model. That
  mechanism is now UNREACHABLE: `resolve_verifier_model` has ZERO callers under `src/rebar`, pinned by
  `test_the_superseded_equality_rule_has_no_production_consumers` (172e). The verifier paths resolve the
  `standard` CLASS instead, so the inversion cannot occur. What remains is narrower and is the real
  subject of this ticket: four code-review steps declare no class at all.
- ~~**Pass-1's ladder routes to the wrong provider.**~~ **RESOLVED — this problem no longer exists, and
  the claim is retained only so the record is honest about what changed.** This section originally read
  that `plan-review.yaml:62-65` sets `model_ladder: [claude-haiku-4-5, claude-sonnet-4-6,
  claude-opus-4-8]` as BARE names, and that since `config.py` maps the `claude` prefix to provider
  `anthropic`, a Bedrock run would send its Pass-1 finders to DIRECT ANTHROPIC — a split brain. VERIFIED
  AT HEAD: that ladder now reads `[trivial, standard, frontier]`, i.e. CLASS terms (story 7761 landed
  it), so the bare-name provider inference no longer applies to plan-review's Pass-1. The split-brain
  risk this ticket was partly created to fix is already closed for plan-review; what REMAINS is the
  code-review gate, below.
- **Code review is only PARTLY split — this is the remaining problem and the reason this ticket is still
  needed.** CORRECTED against HEAD: an earlier version said `code-review.yaml` "declares no `model:` and
  no `model_ladder:` on any step", which is no longer true — `verify` (`:143`) declares `model: standard`
  at `:156` (story 172e landed it). The four steps that still inherit `cfg.model` implicitly are `base`
  (`:67`), `round_a` (`:77`), `round_b` (`:109`) and `coach` (`:182`). So the gate has a Pass-2 split and
  no Pass-1/Pass-4 split. Note the four undeclared steps do NOT fall back to `resolve_verifier_model` either — nothing under
  `src/rebar` calls it. They simply inherit the run's single resolved `cfg.model`, having declared no
  per-step model for the interpreter to override with.

## Why this blocks two stories

- **eb6e (production cutover)** scopes itself to "the bot service's `REBAR_LLM_MODEL`" — one env var
  for four passes. Both single-model outcomes are wrong: opus-everywhere hard-fails Pass-2, which
  pins `temperature=0` (MEASURED: `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` returns 400 `temperature is
  deprecated for this model`; see [rebar:1903-868c-b704-4a80]), and sonnet-everywhere silently
  downgrades Pass-1 with no test to catch it.
- **0d76 (parity bar)** compares v1=Anthropic against v2=Bedrock. Without per-pass control the arms
  differ in TWO variables (provider AND per-pass model class), so any criterion failure is
  unattributable and any pass is unrepresentative of production. A full corpus run is ~3,200 model
  calls; spending that on an unattributable comparison is the expensive way to learn this.

## Approach (the mechanism EXISTS — this ticket is the CONSUMER)

**THE EXACT CLASS EACH STEP DECLARES — stated here so no executor has to guess.** A review round
blocked twice on this being unspecified.

| step | `code-review.yaml` | pass | declares |
|---|---|---|---|
| `base`    | `:67`  | Pass-1 finder (single-shot) | `model: frontier` |
| `round_a` | `:77`  | Pass-1 finder (**batch**)   | inside `batch:` -> `model_ladder: [frontier]` |
| `round_b` | `:109` | Pass-1 finder (**batch**)   | inside `batch:` -> `model_ladder: [frontier]` |
| `verify`  | `:143` | Pass-2 verifier             | `model: standard` — ALREADY LANDED (172e) |
| `coach`   | `:182` | Pass-4 coach                | step-level `model: standard` |

This matches the criterion above — opus-family for Pass-1, sonnet-family for Pass-2/Pass-4 — because
`frontier` and `standard` resolve to exactly those families via `_DEFAULT_MODEL_BY_CLASS`.

**WHY THE BATCH STEPS MUST USE A LADDER KEY, AND WHY IT HAS EXACTLY ONE RUNG.** A step-level `model:` on
a `batch:` step is a SILENT NO-OP — `interpreter.py:384-395` builds `BatchRunRequest` from the `batch:`
sub-dict only (`model_ladder=tuple(batch.get('model_ladder') or ())`) and never passes the enclosing
step's `model:`, while `runners.py:128-130` computes `resolve_model_string(ladder[0]) if ladder else
None` and comments that an empty ladder means "no per-step model, NOT a resolved class". Because `model`
IS a legal step key (`schema.py` `_STEP_ORDER`), such a declaration VALIDATES and is then discarded —
and a test asserting only that the YAML carries a class token would PASS while runtime behaviour was
unchanged. An earlier version of this very table made that mistake.
ONE RUNG, not plan-review's three:
`plan-review.yaml:62-65` declares its finder batch as `model_ladder: [trivial, standard, frontier]`, so
copying that precedent here is the obvious move — and it is the WRONG one for this ticket. A ladder
escalates per criterion, so the model that actually answers a given criterion is NOT determinate: a
cheap criterion may be resolved at `trivial` and never reach `frontier`. This ticket's first criterion
requires a TEST asserting "the RESOLVED model for each pass ... is the intended class", and that
assertion is not writable against a non-deterministic resolution. Flat classes keep the criterion
falsifiable. Adopting the ladder for cost reasons is a legitimate FOLLOW-UP optimisation, but it is a
different change with a different oracle, and bundling it here would make the per-pass guarantee
untestable — which is the whole point of the ticket.

**PASSES vs STEPS — two different counts, both correct, stated so they are not read as a
contradiction.** "Four passes" is the plan-review PASS model (Pass-1 finder, Pass-2 verifier, Pass-3
decide, Pass-4 coach) and is what this ticket's title means. "Five LLM-calling steps" is the CODE-REVIEW
gate's step count in `code-review.yaml`. One pass can be implemented by MORE THAN ONE step — which is
precisely how the batch steps `round_a`/`round_b` escaped an earlier count. Neither number is wrong;
they measure different things.

**REWRITTEN: an earlier draft called this a "candidate, not a decision" and sketched a mapping still to
be designed. Stale — epic eb58 has since shipped it.** `model_classes.py` provides the
trivial/standard/frontier slots, the nine `REBAR_LLM_<CLASS>_<FIELD>` overrides, per-class fallback
chains and class-aware resolution; the batch runners and verifier paths already consume it; and
`REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is deprecated, fanning out to all three classes. This ticket does NOT design a
mapping — it makes the remaining gate steps DECLARE their class.

Make the per-pass model resolvable per provider rather than inferred from one string. Sketch:
express the mapping (Pass-1 finder ladder, Pass-2/Pass-4 verifier) as configuration keyed by
provider, so a Bedrock run names Bedrock inference-profile ids for each pass instead of inheriting
bare `claude-*` names. Note `bedrock_model_id` is NOT the answer — a single scalar cannot express a
mapping, which is part of why it was deleted [rebar:281f-3336-c668-4979].

**STALENESS AUDIT of this section, run against source at HEAD 18ecd9709 rather than accepted wholesale
from a review finding:**
* STALE, fixed: `plan-review.yaml` no longer names bare `claude-*` ids — `:62` declares a `model_ladder`
  in CLASS terms (7761).
* STALE, fixed: "no per-provider class mapping exists" — `model_classes.py` exists and is consumed.
* **RETRACTED — I DEFENDED THIS CLAIM AND IT WAS WRONG.** An earlier revision asserted that
  `review_kernel/verify.py:263-269`'s equality test (`verifier_default if model == default_model else
  ...`) is OPERATIVE, and that steps without a declared class "still inherit the equality rule". The
  function body does still contain that expression — which is all I actually checked — but it has
  **ZERO production call sites**: `resolve_verifier_model` appears under `src/rebar` only as its own
  definition, one docstring mention in `model_classes.py:279`, and two re-export lines in
  `review_kernel/__init__.py`. `tests/unit/test_code_review_verifier_class.py:171`
  (`test_the_superseded_equality_rule_has_no_production_consumers`, landed by 172e) ENFORCES that
  nothing calls it, and instructs "do not relax the assertion". So the rule is superseded and
  unreachable, not live. I verified EXISTENCE and inferred REACHABILITY, which is not the same thing.
* **THE REAL MECHANISM, corrected:** the four undeclared steps inherit the run's single resolved
  `cfg.model` because they declare no per-step model at all — the interpreter simply has nothing to
  override with. That single-knob inheritance is what this ticket removes. `resolve_verifier_model` is
  NOT part of the story and must not be cited as the defect; if anything, a NEW caller of it would
  reintroduce the 172e defect and break the guard test.

This ticket does NOT touch `verify.py:269`. An earlier revision said the chosen shape "must also fix"
that equality test; that instruction rested on the retracted claim above. The helper is superseded and
callerless, a guard test pins it that way, and ADDING a caller would reintroduce the defect 172e
removed. Leave it alone.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a test asserts the RESOLVED model for each pass under a Bedrock configuration is the intended
      class (opus-family for Pass-1, sonnet-family for Pass-2/Pass-4)
- [ ] a test asserts no bare `claude-*` model id is resolved to provider `anthropic` during a run
      configured for another provider
- [ ] a test asserts the Pass-2/Pass-4 downgrade still applies when the operator has NOT explicitly
      chosen a model, on a non-default provider
- [ ] the code-review gate expresses its per-pass models explicitly. RE-MEASURED against the shipped YAML — and this CORRECTS AN ERROR AN EARLIER PASS OF THIS PLAN
      INTRODUCED. That pass wrote "the gate has THREE prompt steps, not four", which is WRONG: it
      counted only the single-shot prompt steps and MISSED THE TWO BATCH STEPS. The gate has FIVE
      LLM-calling steps — `base` (:67), `round_a` (:77), `round_b` (:109), `verify` (:143) and `coach`
      (:182). Only `verify` declares `model: standard` (:156, landed by 172e). The remaining work is
      therefore FOUR steps — `base`, `round_a`, `round_b`, `coach` — all still inheriting `cfg.model`.
      Correcting "four" DOWN to "three" made this plan worse than its original wording, and would
      have shipped two batch steps silently unclassed
- [ ] [operator-attested] a real gate run on the non-default provider shows the per-pass model ids
